fullPassage: While scrolling through her social media one day, Gina was astonished when she saw the news headline, “The Heundeulbawi in Seoraksan National Park Has Fallen.” Gina immediately shared the shocking story with her close friends. Later, during the morning news on TV, a reporter standing next to the undamaged Heundeulbawi said, “Today’s Internet stories of the Heundeulbawi being damaged were fake.” Gina was embarrassed by the fact that she had spread the fake news. It reminded her of another incident of fake news that had happened a while ago. The news that a famous athlete had died became the number one issue online, but it turned out to be fake. It had been made by content creators who sought people’s attention. They produced provocative false stories to make money by raising the number of views of their posts. At that time, Gina criticized those who had made and spread fake news because it had hurt the athlete and confused people. This time, however, Gina herself had accidentally contributed to the spread of fake news. The Impact of Fake News on Society Unfortunately, becoming an accidental distributor of fake news like Gina is not unusual. Fake news is a deliberate attempt to manipulate people by spreading inaccurate information. It is made by certain groups with the intention of attracting people’s attention, making profits, or gaining political benefits. It can confuse people, disturb society, and even seriously harm the public as well as all individuals involved. It is very common for fake news to spread during states of emergency. For example, after an earthquake measuring 6.5 struck Ambon, Indonesia, in September 2019, thousands of residents did not return to their homes and were still in shelters for two weeks. This was because of fake news stories on social media that another earthquake followed by a tsunami was about to strike. One of those messages said, “It’s up to you if you want to believe me or not, but apparently Ambon is going to sink in the next few days.” Many displaced people were so anxious about aftershocks that the government had to announce that the information was fake. The Reasons for the Viral Spread of Fake News Fake news on social media spreads significantly farther and faster than true stories. A study by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the US has shown that fake news spreads online 6 times faster than real news on average. One explanation for this phenomenon is that people like new and provocative things. When information is astonishing, people not only feel that it is surprising, but they also want to share the stimulating news with others. By passing it to others on social media, they can gain attention because they are the first to post previously unknown, but possibly false, information. Also, fake news goes viral because people in their daily lives tend to think simply and effortlessly. It is more likely for them to believe new information without any proof, instead of critically examining it. Moreover, people are inclined to believe information that fits their prejudices or experiences even when not true. In this process, people easily fall into the trap of “confirmation bias.” That is, they selectively accept news in a way that only confirms their beliefs and ignore news that doesn’t support them. During election season, for example, people tend to blindly believe any news describing their favored candidates in a positive way, while unconsciously believing news that reports something negative about other candidates. Ways to Spot and Avoid Fake News With so much information on the Internet, how can you make sure that fake news does not mislead you? First, read beyond the provocative headlines. They can be so stimulating to get more clicks that you may click on them accidentally. So don’t just read the headlines, but read the text carefully. Second, don’t read the news at face value. Exercise critical thinking skills to judge the news. You should question, analyze, and evaluate what you read. Third, examine your biases. Consider if your own beliefs could affect your judgment. Ask yourself if you are only reading articles that suit your opinion, and look for articles that oppose your opinion as well. Finally, check the credibility of the source. You should examine who wrote the news story and what the intent was behind writing the news story. You also need to check whether the news story is from a reliable media source and the evidence is valid. In the digital age, it might be impossible to avoid or eliminate all false information that spreads online. However, if you have the ability to view information critically and objectively, you will be able to reduce the damage that fake news can cause. Don’t forget! Anyone can be the next person producing or spreading fake news! Further Reading Breaking Out of the Echo Chamber These days, everyone accesses the news through the Internet or social media, and often selectively takes the information that suits their tastes or beliefs. However, consistently encountering similar perspectives without considering alternative views can lead you to be trapped in an “echo chamber.” An echo chamber refers to an enclosed space where sound doesn’t leak out and returns as an echo. The term “echo chamber” is also used to describe any situation in which you only hear opinions you already agree with. This can distort your understanding of reality, and limit your ability to think critically and engage in meaningful debates. Worse still, an echo chamber may foster social division, making collaboration on common issues challenging. To avoid falling into this trap, you must actively seek diverse sources of information and engage with people who have different views. Always remember to check the information you receive, and keep an open mind when discussing new ideas. Even if you really want something to be true, it doesn’t always mean that it is true.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ embarrassing → embarrassed: Gina가 '창피함을 느낀' 것이므로 감정을 받는 쪽에 쓰는 과거분사 embarrassed
det.analysis:
① scrolling: 'While scrolling through her social media'는 '소셜 미디어를 넘겨 보다가'라는 뜻이에요. 접속사 While 다음에 '~하는 중'을 나타낼 때 -ing(현재분사)를 써요(While (she was) scrolling). 그래서 scrolling이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② standing: 'a reporter standing next to the undamaged Heundeulbawi'는 '훼손되지 않은 흔들바위 옆에 서 있는 기자'예요. 앞의 명사 reporter를 꾸며 주며 '서 있는'이라고 능동으로 이어 주니 -ing(현재분사) standing이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ embarrassing → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'Gina was embarrassing by the fact'는 '가짜 뉴스를 퍼뜨렸다는 사실에 Gina가 창피했다'라는 뜻이 되어야 해요. 사람이 '창피함을 느낄' 때는 감정을 받는 쪽이라 과거분사 embarrassed(창피한)를 써요. embarrassing(창피하게 만드는)은 남을 창피하게 하는 쪽이라 여기선 어색해요. 그래서 was embarrassed로 고쳐야 맞아요. ❌ embarrassing은 틀림 ←정답

④ happened: 'another incident of fake news that had happened a while ago'는 '얼마 전에 일어났던 또 다른 가짜 뉴스 사건'이에요. 사건이 '일어난' 것은 능동이고, 회상하는 시점보다 더 앞선 과거라 과거완료 had happened가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 감정을 '느끼는' 사람 → 과거분사(-ed): was embarrassed(창피함을 느낀)

Also, fake news ④<u>go</u> viral because people in their daily lives tend to think simply and effortlessly.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ go → goes: 주어 fake news는 단수 취급이라 현재형 동사에 -s를 붙여 goes
det.analysis:
① has shown: 'A study by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the US has shown that~'은 '미국 MIT의 한 연구가 ~을 보여 주었다'예요. 진짜 주어는 'A study(한 연구)' 하나라서 단수예요. 중간에 낀 'by ~ in the US'는 꾸미는 말일 뿐이에요. 그래서 단수 동사 has shown이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② stimulating: 'the stimulating news'는 '자극적인 뉴스'예요. 뉴스가 사람을 '자극하는' 쪽이라 능동의 뜻을 가진 -ing(현재분사) stimulating이 명사 news를 꾸며요. 그래서 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ By passing: 'By passing it to others on social media'는 '그것을 소셜 미디어에서 남들에게 전달함으로써'예요. 전치사 By(~함으로써) 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 쓰니 passing이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ go → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'Also, fake news go viral'은 '또한 가짜 뉴스는 입소문을 탄다'라는 뜻이에요. 주어 fake news는 하나의 덩어리(단수)로 취급하기 때문에 현재형 동사에 -s를 붙여 goes로 써야 해요. go는 복수 주어에 쓰는 형태라 틀려요. ❌ go는 틀림 ←정답
det.tip: fake news는 단수 취급 → 현재형은 goes (news에 이미 s가 있어도 단수)

However, consistently ②<u>encountered</u> similar perspectives without considering alternative views can lead you to be trapped in an “echo chamber. ” An echo chamber ③<u>refers</u> to an enclosed space where sound doesn’t leak out and returns as an echo. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② encountered → encountering: '~하는 것'이라는 동명사 주어라 -ing 형태 encountering
det.analysis:
① accesses: 'everyone accesses the news through the Internet'은 '모두가 인터넷으로 뉴스를 접한다'예요. everyone(모두)은 형태는 여럿 같지만 문법에서는 '한 명 한 명'이라 단수로 취급해요. 그래서 단수 동사 accesses가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② encountered → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'consistently encountering similar perspectives ~ can lead you to be trapped'는 '비슷한 관점을 계속 접하는 것은 당신을 갇히게 만들 수 있다'예요. 문장의 주어가 '~하는 것(접하는 것)'이라 동명사(-ing)로 시작해야 뒤의 동사 can lead와 이어져요. 과거분사 encountered로 쓰면 주어가 만들어지지 않아 문장이 안 돼요. 그래서 encountering으로 고쳐야 맞아요. ❌ encountered는 틀림 ←정답

③ refers: 'An echo chamber refers to an enclosed space'는 '반향실은 밀폐된 공간을 가리킨다'예요. 주어 An echo chamber가 단수라 단수 동사 refers가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ making collaboration: 'an echo chamber may foster social division, making collaboration ~ challenging'은 '반향실은 사회 분열을 조장하고, (그래서) 협력을 어렵게 만든다'예요. 콤마 뒤 making은 '그리고 ~하게 만들면서'라는 뜻을 이어 주는 분사구문(-ing)이라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: '~하는 것'이 주어면 동명사(-ing): Encountering ~ can lead (주어 자리엔 -ing)

questions.passage: It is very common for fake news to spread during states of ①<u>emergency</u>.  For example, after an earthquake measuring 6. 5 struck Ambon, Indonesia, in September 2019, thousands of residents did not return to their homes and were still in shelters for two weeks.  This was because of fake news stories on social media that another earthquake followed by a tsunami was about to ②<u>strike</u>.  One of those messages said, “It’s up to you if you want to believe me or not, but apparently Ambon is going to ③<u>sink</u> in the next few days. ” Many displaced people were so ④<u>calm</u> about aftershocks that the government had to announce that the information was fake.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ calm → anxious: 여진에 대한 가짜 뉴스로 주민들이 '불안해했다'는 흐름이라 anxious
det.analysis:
① emergency: 'It is very common for fake news to spread during states of emergency'는 '가짜 뉴스는 비상 상황에서 퍼지는 일이 매우 흔하다'예요. 바로 뒤에 지진 사례가 나오니 '비상 상황(emergency)'이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② strike: 'another earthquake followed by a tsunami was about to strike'는 '쓰나미를 동반한 또 다른 지진이 곧 닥칠 것'이라는 뜻이에요. 지진이 '덮치다'라는 뜻으로 strike가 맞아요. ✅ 적절

③ sink: 'apparently Ambon is going to sink in the next few days'는 '며칠 안에 암본이 가라앉을 것'이라는 가짜 메시지예요. 사람들을 겁주는 내용이라 '가라앉다(sink)'가 흐름에 맞아요. ✅ 적절

④ calm → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'Many displaced people were so anxious about aftershocks that the government had to announce that the information was fake'로 '많은 이재민이 여진에 대해 너무 불안해해서 정부가 그 정보가 가짜라고 발표해야 했다'예요. 정부가 나서서 진정시켜야 할 만큼 사람들이 '불안해한(anxious)' 상황이지, '차분한(calm)' 상황이 아니에요. calm은 정반대라 문맥에 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: 정부가 '가짜다'라고 발표할 정도 → 사람들은 불안한(anxious) 상태, 차분한(calm) 게 아님

questions.passage: Also, fake news goes viral because people in their daily lives tend to think simply and effortlessly.  It is more likely for them to believe new information without any proof, instead of ①<u>critically</u> examining it.  Moreover, people are ②<u>reluctant</u> to believe information that fits their prejudices or experiences even when not true.  In this process, people easily fall into the ③<u>trap</u> of “confirmation bias. ” That is, they selectively accept news in a way that only confirms their beliefs and ignore news that doesn’t support them.  During election season, for example, people tend to ④<u>blindly</u> believe any news describing their favored candidates in a positive way, while unconsciously believing news that reports something negative about other candidates.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② reluctant → inclined: 사람들은 자기 편견에 맞는 정보를 '믿는 경향이 있다'는 흐름이라 inclined
det.analysis:
① critically: 'instead of critically examining it'은 '그것을 비판적으로 따져 보는 대신'이라는 뜻이에요. 사람들이 증거 없이 정보를 믿는다는 앞 내용과 대비되어 '비판적으로(critically)'가 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② reluctant → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'people are inclined to believe information that fits their prejudices'로 '사람들은 자신의 편견에 맞는 정보를 믿는 경향이 있다'예요. 이 글은 사람들이 편향된 정보를 쉽게 믿는다고 계속 말하고 있으니 '~하는 경향이 있는(inclined)'이 맞아요. reluctant(~하기를 꺼리는)는 정반대 뜻이라 문맥에 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답

③ trap: 'people easily fall into the trap of confirmation bias'는 '사람들이 확증 편향의 함정에 쉽게 빠진다'예요. 잘못된 사고 습관을 '함정(trap)'에 비유한 것이라 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

④ blindly: 'people tend to blindly believe any news describing their favored candidates in a positive way'는 '자신이 지지하는 후보를 긍정적으로 그리는 뉴스를 맹목적으로 믿는 경향이 있다'예요. 따져 보지 않고 믿는다는 뜻이라 '맹목적으로(blindly)'가 맞아요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: 편향된 정보를 쉽게 믿는다는 글의 흐름 → inclined(~하는 경향이 있는), reluctant(꺼리는)는 반대

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ simply and effortlessly(단순하고 힘 안 들이게): 사람들이 깊이 따지지 않고 대충 생각한다는 흐름
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'fake news goes viral because people in their daily lives tend to think ___'(가짜 뉴스가 퍼지는 이유는 사람들이 일상에서 ___ 생각하는 경향이 있기 때문이다). 바로 뒤 문장에서 '증거도 없이 새 정보를 믿고, 비판적으로 따져 보지 않는다'고 했어요. 즉 사람들은 깊이 생각하지 않고 '단순하고 힘 안 들이게' 생각한다는 뜻이 되어야 해요.

❌ ① slowly and carefully(천천히 그리고 신중하게): 신중히 따진다는 뜻이라, 대충 믿는다는 뒤 내용과 반대예요.

❌ ② logically and rationally(논리적으로 그리고 이성적으로): 이성적으로 판단한다는 뜻이라 흐름과 안 맞아요.

✅ ③ simply and effortlessly(단순하고 힘 안 들이게): 증거 없이 대충 믿는다는 뒤 내용과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ④ deeply and objectively(깊고 객관적으로): 깊이 파고든다는 뜻이라, 대충 생각한다는 흐름과 반대예요.
det.tip: 뒤 문장 '증거 없이 믿고 비판적으로 안 따진다' → 생각을 '단순하고 힘 안 들이게' 한다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① opinions you already agree with(당신이 이미 동의하는 의견들): 반향실은 같은 생각만 되돌려 주는 공간
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'The term echo chamber is also used to describe any situation in which you only hear ___'(반향실이라는 말은 당신이 오직 ___ 만 듣는 상황을 묘사할 때도 쓰인다). 앞에서 반향실은 '자기 취향에 맞는 정보만 골라 받아들이는' 공간이라고 했어요. 즉 이미 동의하는 의견만 듣는 상황이에요.

✅ ① opinions you already agree with(당신이 이미 동의하는 의견들): 같은 생각만 되돌아온다는 반향실의 정의와 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ② arguments that oppose your beliefs(당신의 믿음에 반대하는 주장들): 오히려 반향실에서 '빠져나오는' 방법이라, 정의와 반대예요.

❌ ③ news from unfamiliar experts(낯선 전문가들의 뉴스): 낯선 정보를 듣는다는 뜻이라 흐름과 안 맞아요.

❌ ④ voices from the other side(반대편의 목소리): 다른 편 의견을 듣는다는 뜻이라, 같은 의견만 듣는다는 정의와 반대예요.
det.tip: 반향실 = 메아리처럼 '이미 동의하는 의견'만 되돌아오는 공간

questions.passage: While scrolling through her social media one day, Gina was astonished when she saw the news headline, “The Heundeulbawi in Seoraksan National Park Has Fallen. ” Gina immediately shared the shocking story with her close friends.  Later, during the morning news on TV, a reporter standing next to the undamaged Heundeulbawi said, “Today’s Internet stories of the Heundeulbawi being damaged were fake. ” Gina was embarrassed by the fact that she had spread the fake news.  It reminded her of another incident of fake news that had happened a while ago.  The news that a famous athlete had died became the number one issue online, but it turned out to be fake.  It had been made by content creators who sought people’s attention.  They produced provocative false stories to make money by raising the number of views of their posts.  At that time, Gina criticized those who had made and spread fake news because it had hurt the athlete and confused people.  This time, however, Gina herself had accidentally contributed to the spread of fake news.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문 근거: Gina was embarrassed by the fact that she had spread the fake news
det.analysis:
❌ ① 원문은 'Gina immediately shared the shocking story with her close friends'로, Gina가 그 소식을 즉시 친구들에게 공유했어요. '알리지 않았다'는 반대예요.

❌ ② 원문에서 기자는 'standing next to the undamaged Heundeulbawi'(훼손되지 않은 흔들바위 옆에 서서) '오늘 인터넷 이야기들은 가짜였다'고 말했어요. 실제로 훼손됐다고 전한 것이 아니라 가짜라고 바로잡았어요.

❌ ③ 원문은 'The news that a famous athlete had died ~ turned out to be fake'로, 운동선수가 죽었다는 뉴스는 '가짜로 밝혀졌다'고 했어요. 사실로 밝혀진 것이 아니에요.

✅ ④ 원문 'Gina was embarrassed by the fact that she had spread the fake news'(자신이 가짜 뉴스를 퍼뜨렸다는 사실에 Gina는 당황했다)와 일치해요. ←정답
det.tip: 함정: 기자는 '가짜'라고 바로잡음 / 운동선수 뉴스도 '가짜'로 판명

ch: Gina는 헤드라인을 보고도 대수롭지 않게 여겨 친구들에게 알리지 않았다.
TV 아침 뉴스의 기자는 흔들바위가 실제로 훼손되었다고 전했다.
한 유명 운동선수가 사망했다는 뉴스는 결국 사실로 밝혀졌다.
Gina는 자신이 가짜 뉴스를 퍼뜨렸다는 사실에 당황했다.

questions.passage: The Impact of Fake News on Society Unfortunately, becoming an accidental distributor of fake news like Gina is not unusual.  Fake news is a deliberate attempt to manipulate people by spreading inaccurate information.  It is made by certain groups with the intention of attracting people’s attention, making profits, or gaining political benefits.  It can confuse people, disturb society, and even seriously harm the public as well as all individuals involved.  It is very common for fake news to spread during states of emergency.  For example, after an earthquake measuring 6. 5 struck Ambon, Indonesia, in September 2019, thousands of residents did not return to their homes and were still in shelters for two weeks.  This was because of fake news stories on social media that another earthquake followed by a tsunami was about to strike.  One of those messages said, “It’s up to you if you want to believe me or not, but apparently Ambon is going to sink in the next few days. ” Many displaced people were so anxious about aftershocks that the government had to announce that the information was fake.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문: 주민들이 대피소에 머문 것은 '또 지진·쓰나미가 온다'는 가짜 뉴스 때문 (정부 명령 아님)
det.analysis:
❌ ① 이 진술은 본문과 일치해요. 원문 'It is made by certain groups with the intention of ~'(특정 집단이 ~하려는 의도로 만든다)와 맞아요.

❌ ② 이 진술은 본문과 일치해요. 원문 'thousands of residents did not return to their homes and were still in shelters for two weeks'(수천 명의 주민이 집에 돌아가지 못하고 2주 동안 대피소에 있었다)와 맞아요.

✅ ③ 여기가 정답(일치하지 않는 것)! 원문은 'This was because of fake news stories on social media that another earthquake followed by a tsunami was about to strike'로, 주민들이 대피소에 머문 이유는 '또 다른 지진과 쓰나미가 온다'는 가짜 뉴스 때문이었어요. 정부의 공식 대피 명령 때문이 아니에요. 오히려 정부는 그 정보가 가짜라고 발표했어요. ←정답

❌ ④ 이 진술은 본문과 일치해요. 원문 'It is very common for fake news to spread during states of emergency'(가짜 뉴스는 비상 상황에서 퍼지는 일이 흔하다)와 맞아요.
det.tip: 대피소에 머문 진짜 이유 = 가짜 뉴스(추가 지진·쓰나미 소문), 정부 명령이 아님

ch: 가짜 뉴스는 특정 집단이 어떤 의도를 가지고 만들어 낸다.
인도네시아 암본에서는 지진 후 많은 주민이 2주 동안 대피소에 머물렀다.
주민들이 대피소에 머문 것은 정부의 공식 대피 명령 때문이었다.
가짜 뉴스는 비상 상황에서 퍼지는 경우가 흔하다.

questions.passage: Ways to Spot and Avoid Fake News With so much information on the Internet, how can you make sure that fake news does not mislead you?  First, read beyond the provocative headlines.  They can be so stimulating to get more clicks that you may click on them accidentally.  So don’t just read the headlines, but read the text carefully.  Second, don’t read the news at face value.  Exercise critical thinking skills to judge the news.  You should question, analyze, and evaluate what you read.  Third, examine your biases.  Consider if your own beliefs could affect your judgment.  Ask yourself if you are only reading articles that suit your opinion, and look for articles that oppose your opinion as well.  Finally, check the credibility of the source.  You should examine who wrote the news story and what the intent was behind writing the news story.  You also need to check whether the news story is from a reliable media source and the evidence is valid.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ① 원문 근거: look for articles that oppose your opinion as well
det.analysis:
✅ ① 원문 'Ask yourself if you are only reading articles that suit your opinion, and look for articles that oppose your opinion as well'(자기 의견에 맞는 기사만 읽고 있는지 자문하고, 반대되는 기사도 찾아보라)와 일치해요. ←정답

❌ ② 원문은 'don't just read the headlines, but read the text carefully'로, 헤드라인만 읽지 말고 본문을 꼼꼼히 읽으라고 했어요. 헤드라인만 빠르게 읽으라는 건 반대예요.

❌ ③ 원문은 'don't read the news at face value. Exercise critical thinking skills'로, 액면 그대로 믿지 말고 비판적 사고를 하라고 했어요. 반대예요.

❌ ④ 원문 'check the credibility of the source. You should examine who wrote the news story ~'로, 출처와 작성자를 확인하라고 했어요. 확인할 필요가 없다는 건 반대예요.
det.tip: 이 글의 핵심 조언 = 반대 의견 기사도 찾아 읽고, 출처·본문을 비판적으로 확인하라

ch: 자신의 의견과 반대되는 기사도 찾아 읽어 볼 필요가 있다.
가짜 뉴스를 피하려면 자극적인 헤드라인만 빠르게 읽으면 된다.
뉴스는 비판적 사고 없이 액면 그대로 받아들이는 것이 좋다.
뉴스의 출처나 작성자는 굳이 확인할 필요가 없다.

questions.passage: The Reasons for the Viral Spread of Fake News Fake news on social media spreads significantly farther and faster than true stories.  A study by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the US has shown that fake news spreads online 6 times faster than real news on average.  One explanation for this phenomenon is that people like new and provocative things.  When information is astonishing, people not only feel that it is surprising, but they also want to share the stimulating news with others.  By passing it to others on social media, they can gain attention because they are the first to post previously unknown, but possibly false, information.  Also, fake news goes viral because people in their daily lives tend to think simply and effortlessly.  It is more likely for them to believe new information without any proof, instead of critically examining it.  Moreover, people are inclined to believe information that fits their prejudices or experiences even when not true.  In this process, people easily fall into the trap of “confirmation bias. ” That is, they selectively accept news in a way that only confirms their beliefs and ignore news that doesn’t support them.  During election season, for example, people tend to blindly believe any news describing their favored candidates in a positive way, while unconsciously believing news that reports something negative about other candidates.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② 이 부분은 가짜 뉴스가 왜 진짜 뉴스보다 빠르고 멀리 퍼지는지 그 이유를 설명하는 글이에요
det.analysis:
글의 첫머리에서 '가짜 뉴스는 진짜 이야기보다 훨씬 멀리, 빠르게 퍼진다', 'MIT 연구에 따르면 평균 6배 빠르다'고 했어요. 이어서 그 이유로 ① 사람들이 새롭고 자극적인 것을 좋아하고, ② 깊이 생각하지 않으며, ③ 자기 편견에 맞는 정보만 믿는 '확증 편향'에 빠진다는 점을 들어요.

❌ ③ 소셜 미디어 사용 시간을 줄이는 방법은 다루지 않아요.

❌ ④ 선거 후보 선택 기준은 확증 편향을 설명하는 예시일 뿐, 글의 주제가 아니에요.
det.tip: 핵심 = 가짜 뉴스가 빨리 퍼지는 '이유'(새로움 선호·안이한 사고·확증 편향)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② new and provocative things(새롭고 자극적인 것들): 사람들이 새 자극을 좋아해 가짜 뉴스가 퍼진다는 설명
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'One explanation for this phenomenon is that people like ___'(이 현상에 대한 한 가지 설명은 사람들이 ___ 을 좋아한다는 것이다). 바로 뒤 문장에서 '정보가 놀라울 때 사람들은 그 자극적인 뉴스를 남과 나누고 싶어 한다'고 했어요. 즉 사람들이 좋아하는 것은 '새롭고 자극적인 것'이에요.

❌ ① old and familiar stories(오래되고 익숙한 이야기들): '새로운' 것을 좋아한다는 뒤 내용과 반대예요.

✅ ② new and provocative things(새롭고 자극적인 것들): 뒤 문장의 '놀랍고 자극적인 뉴스'와 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ calm and predictable facts(차분하고 예측 가능한 사실들): 자극적인 것과 반대라 흐름에 안 맞아요.

❌ ④ boring and ordinary details(지루하고 평범한 세부 사항): 사람들이 좋아할 이유가 없어 흐름과 반대예요.
det.tip: 뒤 문장의 'surprising·stimulating news' 단서 → 사람들은 '새롭고 자극적인 것'을 좋아함

questions.passage: Second, don’t read the news at face value.  __________.  You should question, analyze, and evaluate what you read.  Third, examine your biases.  Consider if your own beliefs could affect your judgment.  Ask yourself if you are only reading articles that suit your opinion, and look for articles that oppose your opinion as well.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"뉴스를 판단하기 위해 비판적 사고 능력을 발휘하라." (8단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) critical, Exercise, judge, news, skills, the, thinking, to 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: Exercise critical thinking skills to judge the news
det.analysis:
'~을 발휘하라'라는 명령문이라 동사원형 Exercise(발휘하라)로 시작해요.

무엇을 발휘하는가 하면 목적어 'critical thinking skills(비판적 사고 능력)'예요. 꾸미는 말 순서는 critical(비판적) → thinking(사고) → skills(능력)로 놓아요.

'뉴스를 판단하기 위해'는 목적을 나타내는 to부정사로 나타내요: to judge(판단하기 위해) + the news(뉴스를).

순서대로 이으면 Exercise / critical / thinking / skills / to / judge / the / news → 'Exercise critical thinking skills to judge the news'.
det.tip: 명령문 = 동사원형으로 시작(Exercise) / 목적 '~하기 위해'는 to부정사(to judge)

questions.wa: Exercise critical thinking skills to judge the news
accept: Exercise critical thinking skills to judge the news

questions.passage: The Impact of Fake News on Society Unfortunately, becoming an accidental distributor of fake news like Gina is not unusual.  Fake news is a deliberate attempt to manipulate people by spreading inaccurate information.  It is made by certain groups with the intention of ①<u>to attract</u> people’s attention, making profits, or gaining political benefits.  It can confuse people, disturb society, and even seriously harm the public as well as all individuals involved.  It is very common for fake news to spread during states of emergency.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: to attract → attracting: 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 쓰고, 뒤의 making·gaining과 형태를 맞춰야 하므로 attracting
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장은 'It is made by certain groups with the intention of ①<u>to attract</u> people's attention, making profits, or gaining political benefits.'예요. '특정 집단이 사람들의 관심을 끌거나, 이익을 얻거나, 정치적 이득을 얻으려는 의도로 만든다'라는 뜻이에요.

먼저 'of'는 전치사예요. 전치사 뒤에는 동사를 그대로 못 쓰고 동명사(-ing)로 바꿔 써야 해요. 그래서 to attract가 아니라 attracting이 되어야 해요.

또 뒤에 이어지는 'making profits, or gaining political benefits'를 보면 모두 -ing 형태예요. 'A, B, or C'처럼 나란히 이어지는 말은 형태를 똑같이 맞춰야 해요(병렬 구조). 그래서 attracting / making / gaining으로 통일해야 맞아요.

따라서 to attract를 attracting으로 고쳐야 해요.
det.tip: 전치사(of) 뒤 + 병렬(making, gaining)에 맞춤 → attracting

questions.passage: It reminded her of another incident of fake news that had happened a while ago.  __________, but it turned out to be fake.  It had been made by content creators who sought people’s attention.  They produced provocative false stories to make money by raising the number of views of their posts.  At that time, Gina criticized those who had made and spread fake news because it had hurt the athlete and confused people.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"한 유명 운동선수가 사망했다는 뉴스가 온라인에서 가장 큰 이슈가 되었다." (14단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) a, athlete, became, died, famous, had, issue, news, number, one, online, that, the, The 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 14단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: The news that a famous athlete had died became the number one issue online
det.analysis:
문장의 진짜 주어는 'The news(그 뉴스)'예요. 어떤 뉴스인지 설명이 필요하니, 'that a famous athlete had died(한 유명 운동선수가 사망했다는)'를 the news 바로 뒤에 붙여요. 여기서 that은 '~라는'의 뜻으로 내용을 이어 주는 접속사예요.

'사망했다'는 뉴스가 화제가 되기 이전의 일이라, 한 시제 앞선 과거완료 'had died'로 써요.

주어가 길게 끝난 뒤 동사 'became(~이 되었다)'을 놓고, 'the number one issue(가장 큰 이슈)'를 이어요: the → number → one → issue.

마지막에 '온라인에서'를 뜻하는 online을 붙여요.

순서대로 이으면 The / news / that / a / famous / athlete / had / died / became / the / number / one / issue / online.
det.tip: the news that + 문장 = '~라는 뉴스' / 더 앞선 과거는 과거완료(had died)

questions.wa: The news that a famous athlete had died became the number one issue online
accept: The news that a famous athlete had died became the number one issue online

questions.passage: The term “echo chamber” is also used to describe any situation in which you only hear opinions you already agree with.  This can distort your understanding of reality, and limit your ability to think critically and engage in meaningful debates.  Worse still, an echo chamber may foster social division, making collaboration on common issues challenging.  To avoid falling into this trap, you must actively seek diverse sources of information and engage with people who have different views.  __________, and keep an open mind when discussing new ideas.  Even if you really want something to be true, it doesn’t always mean that it is true.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
"당신이 받는 정보를 항상 확인하는 것을 기억하라."

[ Always / check / information / receive / remember / the / to / you ] (8단어) (영어로)

det.korean: Always remember to check the information you receive
det.analysis:
'항상 ~하는 것을 기억하라'라는 명령문이에요. 먼저 '항상'을 뜻하는 Always를 맨 앞에 놓고, 명령문의 동사원형 remember(기억하라)를 이어요.

remember 뒤에 '~할 것을'은 to부정사로 나타내요: to check(확인하는 것을).

무엇을 확인하는가 하면 'the information(그 정보)'이에요. 그리고 '당신이 받는'이라는 꾸미는 말이 information을 뒤에서 설명해요: (that) you receive. 관계대명사 that이 생략된 형태라 you receive를 바로 붙여요.

순서대로 이으면 Always / remember / to / check / the / information / you / receive → 'Always remember to check the information you receive'.
det.tip: 명령문 Always + 동사원형 / 'the information (that) you receive' = 당신이 받는 정보

questions.wa: Always remember to check the information you receive
accept: Always remember to check the information you receive

questions.passage: Third, examine your biases.  __________.  Ask yourself if you are only reading articles that suit your opinion, and look for articles that oppose your opinion as well.  Finally, check the credibility of the source.  You should examine who wrote the news story and what the intent was behind writing the news story.  You also need to check whether the news story is from a reliable media source and the evidence is valid.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"당신 자신의 신념이 당신의 판단에 영향을 줄 수 있는지 생각해 보라." (9단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) affect, beliefs, Consider, could, if, judgment, own, your, your 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: Consider if your own beliefs could affect your judgment
det.analysis:
'~인지 생각해 보라'라는 명령문이라 동사원형 Consider(생각해 보라)로 시작해요.

'~인지'는 '그런지 아닌지'를 뜻하는 접속사 if(=whether)로 이어요: Consider if ~(~인지 생각해 보라).

if가 이끄는 내용의 주어는 'your own beliefs(당신 자신의 신념)'예요. own은 '자신의'라는 뜻으로 your 바로 뒤에 붙여 강조해요: your → own → beliefs.

'영향을 줄 수 있는지'는 조동사 could(~할 수 있다) + 동사원형 affect(영향을 주다)로 나타내요: could → affect.

무엇에 영향을 주는가 하면 'your judgment(당신의 판단)'예요.

순서대로 이으면 Consider / if / your / own / beliefs / could / affect / your / judgment.
det.tip: 명령문 Consider + if(=whether, ~인지) / your own beliefs = 당신 자신의 신념

questions.wa: Consider if your own beliefs could affect your judgment
accept: Consider if your own beliefs could affect your judgment
